clue.text: European staff

blocks.note: first meaning: a native of Poland
second meaning: a long rod or stick

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the workforce of a European firm, but staff here is a stick, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pole is a person from Poland, and a pole is a long wooden rod, the same spelling serving both meanings.

clue.text: Begin lifting setter: what might setter do?

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting something raises it, so its letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the setter of the puzzle refers to themself as me
this time the setter is the dog breed, and a dog barks

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler wonders aloud what to do next while starting to raise themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter is used twice: first as the crossword compiler (ME), then as the gundog. The question mark flags the switch.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark on something is to start or commence it, as when one sets out on a journey or project.

clue.text: Nasty cold consuming kid at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter of the word
to consume is to swallow up, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: icy means very cold
the opening letter of kid

explanation.surface: A child has caught a horrible cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold looks like a noun for an illness, but it is the adjective ICY, which wraps around the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky is informal for unpleasant or sticky and distasteful, so it serves as a synonym for something disagreeable.

clue.text: Middle Eastern country holding territorials up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the letters read from the bottom to the top
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a Middle Eastern country
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Gulf state is holding up a group of reservist soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The country in the wordplay is not the answer's own country: it is a neighbour, turned upside down around TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatari is the adjective for things belonging to Qatar, a state on the Persian Gulf in the Middle East.

clue.text: Calm as a silent dove, you might say, bearing north

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it within, so one piece holds another

blocks.clueFragment: a silent dove, you might say
blocks.note: a dove that makes no coo could be jokingly called coo-less
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone is as serene as a quiet dove, facing north.
explanation.walkthrough: You might say marks an invented word: a dove without its coo is coo-less, and N goes inside it after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolness as a noun means composure or unflappability, the state of staying unruffled under pressure.

clue.text: Place on racecourse where £1,000 put on hack

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing put on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
to hack something, as in 'I can't hack it', is to tolerate it

explanation.surface: At the races, a punter puts a thousand pounds on a tired old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A hack is also a worn-out horse, which suits the racing picture; here it is the verb meaning to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: The grandstand is the main covered seating structure at a racecourse from which spectators watch the races.

clue.text: Cold: most ice melting on the surface

indicators.note: something melting loses its shape and reforms, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chilly scene where nearly all the ice is thawing at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'on the surface' as where the ice melts, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic change is superficial, affecting only outward appearance rather than anything deeper or substantial.

clue.text: Unlikely youth will lose out over old cry of the hunt

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so letters are removed
in a down answer, what is over another sits above it, so comes first

blocks.note: as in a tall story, one hard to believe
the word youth with its middle three letters removed
the letters removed from the previous word
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An improbable young person will give up on a traditional hunting call.
explanation.walkthrough: Out is not an indicator here: it names the very letters the youth loses, leaving Y and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the traditional shout a huntsman gives on sighting a fox, urging the hounds and riders onward.

clue.text: A plank on ship

blocks.note: taken as written
a plank is a long flat length of timber

explanation.surface: A single timber plank lies on the deck of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a single timber on a vessel; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or onto a vessel, so a passenger who is on ship is aboard.

clue.text: Come off line: redial anew

indicators.note: doing something anew means making it over again differently, so the letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A phone call has dropped, so the caller dials the number again.
explanation.walkthrough: Line looks like a telephone line, which fits redial; it is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A train derails when its wheels leave the track, so derail means to run off the rails.

clue.text: Horse in a grey, luck initially out

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
the opening letter of luck

explanation.surface: A grey racehorse is out of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: In a grey reads as a description of the horse's colour, but its letters are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, between one and two years old, especially a racehorse.

clue.text: Financial concern about king mucking about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: financial means to do with money
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: A money worry about the monarch who is fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: Financial concern looks like a single worry, but it is a money business, with the king inserted into the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for mischievous or silly behaviour, much like fooling around or horseplay.

clue.text: Store lacking in commodities originally overwhelmed by shoplifting, say?

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so the first letter of each word is taken
something overwhelmed is engulfed, so it ends up surrounded by another piece

blocks.note: shoplifting is an example of a crime; say marks an example
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A shop that has run out of goods is hit by a wave of shoplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lacking looks like the main verb of the sentence, but it only supplies its first letter. An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-licence is a retail shop selling alcoholic drinks for consumption elsewhere, so it is a kind of shop.

clue.text: Out of bed and ready for surprise

blocks.note: someone out of bed is up
as in ready, steady, go: get set

explanation.surface: Someone is awake, dressed and prepared for whatever shock comes.
explanation.walkthrough: Surprise is the noun here: a sporting result nobody expected.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is an unexpected result, such as an underdog beating the favourite, which is a shock outcome.

clue.text: One or two cafe workers, though no corkers!

indicators.note: having none of something means those letters are taken away from the rest

blocks.note: taken letter for letter; that the survivors sit together inside it is no coincidence, since the removed letters are the first one and the last six
these letters are removed: one from the front of the first phrase, six from its end

explanation.surface: A café has only a couple of staff, and none of them is outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: Corkers looks like an insult about the staff; it is the set of letters to strike out, which are scattered rather than together. A corker is British slang for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A few means a small number, a handful, which is how one or two is loosely used.

clue.text: Awful, heartless war made a deep impression

indicators.note: without its heart a word keeps only the outside letters

blocks.note: war with its middle letter gone
to etch is to cut a deep mark into a surface

explanation.surface: A cruel and terrible war left a lasting mark on people.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartless reads as cruel, describing the war, but it removes the middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched means very bad or miserable in quality, so it serves as a synonym for dreadful or terrible.

clue.text: Refuge required in Tokyo, as I said

indicators.note: in means within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the city name and the next three words

explanation.surface: Someone repeats that they need shelter in Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: Tokyo suggests a Japanese word, but the answer runs on from its last letter into the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert and figuratively any place of calm retreat or sanctuary.

clue.text: Supporter carrying father up in small plane, say?

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: a sling supports an injured arm
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone carries their dad aloft in a light aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Plane looks like an aeroplane; it is the plane tree, and say flags it as one example of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, so a small plane tree is an example of one.

clue.text: Change hands, switched over

indicators.note: to switch something over is to turn it round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: paws are informal hands

explanation.surface: Something changes owner, passing from one person to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Change hands reads as one phrase about ownership, but the definition stops after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, which is a straightforward synonym for change as a verb.

clue.text: Error in data entry I spied, not small – row of figures to look at?

definitions.text: row of figures to look at?

indicators.note: an error puts things in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so these letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone notices a mistake in data entry, a row of figures in a spreadsheet.
explanation.walkthrough: Row of figures suggests numbers in a table; the figures are people standing in a line for a witness to inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity parade is a police line-up of people, viewed by a witness who tries to pick out a suspect.

clue.text: Lead: it could be followed

indicators.note: could be suggests a possible alternative form, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to take the front, so others can follow behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead and followed look like opposites in a single picture; lead is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them secretly, as a detective trails a suspect, so tailed means followed.

clue.text: Story on drink

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A tale about drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: On here is RE, meaning about or concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a news story or account of events, so the two words are synonyms in journalism.

clue.text: Adorable skill of dog in park?

blocks.note: first meaning: attractive, charming
second meaning: retrieving a thrown stick or ball, what a dog does in a park

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like praise of a cute dog's trick; one word is both the charm and the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching is an adjective meaning attractive, and also the act of retrieving something thrown, a classic canine trick.

clue.text: Great being around a source of provocation

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a deity is a great being
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mighty creature hovers about whatever stirs things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Great being reads as an adjective and verb; it is a noun phrase for a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A goad is a pointed stick for driving cattle, and figuratively anything that spurs or provokes someone to act.

clue.text: Devil appearing like an animal

blocks.note: an imp is a small devil
à la, from French, means in the style of

explanation.surface: A demon looks like a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Like gives ALA, the French phrase à la meaning in the manner of.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Idle thinker

blocks.note: first meaning: to laze about, a verb
second meaning: the head, via Cockney rhyming slang on bread

explanation.walkthrough: Idle thinker sounds like a daydreamer. In Cockney rhyming slang loaf of bread means head, so 'use your loaf' means think.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to lounge around doing nothing, and loaf is slang for the head, the organ one thinks with.

clue.text: Plot in story can help explain my emotions, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.clueFragment: story can help explain my emotions
blocks.note: the opening letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A writer hopes a novel's storyline can express their feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot looks like the storyline of the tale, which fits the surface; it is a secret plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a cunning plan or conspiracy, so it matches plot in the sense of an intrigue.

clue.text: African billionaire gladly provided backing, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so just part of the words is used
backing means moving backwards, so the letters read in reverse order

blocks.note: the letters lie across the end of the first word and the start of the second, read right to left

explanation.surface: A rich man from Africa was happy to fund a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing reads as financial support, fitting the billionaire, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An Algerian is a person from Algeria, a country in North Africa, so an example of an African.
